court: Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

issues.label: Final agency action reviewable
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Plan and master permits are final agency actions subject to judicial review.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm it has jurisdiction under the ESA citizen-suit provision and/or APA and any other jurisdictional bases.

issues.label: APA cause of action
issues.why: If proceeding under the APA, court must determine plaintiffs challenge a reviewable agency action and satisfy APA prerequisites.

issues.label: Standing (Article III)
issues.why: Plaintiffs must show injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability for ESA/NEPA claims.

issues.label: Organizational standing
issues.why: Court must assess whether Friends of Animals has associational or organizational standing based on members’ use and interests.

issues.label: Mootness and ripeness
issues.why: Court must determine whether the dispute is ripe and not moot given permit terms, ongoing actions, or expired/changed circumstances.

issues.label: Statute of limitations
issues.why: Court must determine whether claims are timely under the applicable limitations period (often APA six-year) and accrual rules.

issues.label: Venue and service issues
issues.why: Court must confirm proper venue and compliance with any notice/service prerequisites.

issues.label: Exhaustion of remedies
issues.why: Court must decide whether administrative exhaustion is required and, if so, satisfied or excused.

issues.label: Scope of record review
issues.why: Court must define the administrative record and whether supplementation or extra-record evidence is permissible.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: Court must apply the correct standard (typically APA arbitrary-and-capricious/substantial evidence) to ESA/NEPA determinations.

issues.label: Deference to agency interpretations
issues.why: Court must decide what deference, if any, applies to the Service’s interpretations of ESA/NEPA regulations and the Plan.

issues.label: Remedy availability
issues.why: Court must determine available remedies (vacatur, injunction, remand) and equitable factors.

issues.label: Severability of permits/plan
issues.why: Court must decide whether flaws require vacating the whole Plan/permits or only discrete portions.

issues.label: ESA incidental take permit authority
issues.why: Court must confirm the Service had statutory authority to issue incidental take permits for a threatened species in this context.

issues.label: Use of master permits
issues.why: Court must decide whether issuing county master permits with certificates of inclusion is lawful under ESA §10 and regulations.

issues.label: Permit issuance procedures
issues.why: Court must determine whether required procedural steps for permit issuance (notice, comment, findings) were followed.

issues.label: §10(a)(2)(A) plan requirements met
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether a legally adequate conservation plan accompanied the permits.

issues.label: Max extent practicable mitigation
issues.why: Court must decide whether minimization and mitigation were to the maximum extent practicable as required by §10(a)(2)(B)(ii).

issues.label: Funding assured
issues.why: Court must assess whether the Service reasonably found funding would be provided to implement mitigation and monitoring.

issues.label: No appreciable reduction finding
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the permits would not appreciably reduce survival and recovery likelihood under §10(a)(2)(B)(iv).

issues.label: Other necessary measures
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Service required all “necessary or appropriate” measures to implement the plan.

issues.label: Incidental take scope and limits
issues.why: Court must determine whether authorized take levels (up to 7,152) are supported and appropriately bounded.

issues.label: Enforceability of mitigation
issues.why: Court must assess whether mitigation duties (translocation, banks, easements) are enforceable permit conditions rather than aspirational.

issues.label: Monitoring and adaptive management
issues.why: Court must decide whether monitoring and annual review are adequate to ensure mitigation success and compliance.

issues.label: Translocation adequacy
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether translocation and colony establishment are scientifically supported and likely to offset impacts.

issues.label: Mitigation ratios and equivalency
issues.why: Court must assess whether mitigation fully offsets take and whether equivalency assumptions are rational and evidence-based.

issues.label: Mitigation on federal/protected lands
issues.why: Court must determine legality and adequacy of relying on federal/protected lands for establishing new colonies and long-term management.

issues.label: Conservation banks/easements adequacy
issues.why: Court must evaluate permanence, management commitments, and ecological sufficiency of banks, acquisitions, and easements.

issues.label: Baseline and cumulative effects
issues.why: Court must ensure the Service considered baseline conditions and cumulative impacts when concluding no appreciable reduction/offset.

issues.label: Use of historical averages projections
issues.why: Court must decide whether projecting habitat loss from historical averages is rational given acknowledged growth uncertainty.

issues.label: Consideration of higher-growth scenario
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether analyzing fivefold development adequately brackets foreseeable risk and uncertainty.

issues.label: Treatment of uncertainty/risk
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Service adequately addressed scientific uncertainty and risk of mitigation failure.

issues.label: Reliance on low-quality habitat labels
issues.why: Court must assess whether habitat-quality classifications are supported and not used to understate impacts.

issues.label: Development area designations validity
issues.why: Court must decide whether major/minor development area definitions and mapping are reasonable and supported by the record.

issues.label: Non-federal land limitation
issues.why: Court must evaluate implications of excluding federal lands from development designations and impact calculations.

issues.label: Geographic scope (7 counties)
issues.why: Court must assess whether Plan’s geographic coverage is appropriate for the species’ range and impacts.

issues.label: Recovery units significance
issues.why: Court must determine whether recovery-unit designations were properly used in evaluating impacts and recovery.

issues.label: Effects on survival vs recovery
issues.why: Court must ensure the Service analyzed both survival and recovery impacts, not merely short-term persistence.

issues.label: Jeopardy vs §10 standard clarity
issues.why: Court must address whether reliance on “no jeopardy” language improperly substitutes for the §10 “no appreciable reduction” standard.

issues.label: Consistency with §4(d) rule
issues.why: Court must determine whether threatened-species take prohibition and any special 4(d) rules affect permitting and conditions.

issues.label: Take definition application
issues.why: Court must assess whether habitat destruction and authorized activities constitute “take” and are properly covered by permits.

issues.label: Third-party developer coverage
issues.why: Court must decide whether certificates of inclusion properly extend permit coverage to multiple developers and activities.

issues.label: County authority and discretion
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether counties’ role in issuing certificates is consistent with ESA requirements and federal oversight.

issues.label: Permit term and reinitiation triggers
issues.why: Court must examine whether ten-year term and any triggers for modification/revocation are adequate under law.

issues.label: Changed circumstances provisions
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Plan adequately addresses changed/unforeseen circumstances and contingency measures.

issues.label: Compliance and enforcement mechanisms
issues.why: Court must assess whether there are adequate compliance checks, reporting, and enforcement for permittees and developers.

issues.label: NEPA applicability
issues.why: Court must determine whether issuing the Plan and master permits is a “major federal action” triggering NEPA.

issues.label: NEPA document type proper
issues.why: Court must decide whether an EA/FONSI was lawful or whether an EIS was required.

issues.label: Significance determination (FONSI)
issues.why: Court must assess whether the Service reasonably found no significant environmental impact given scale of take and habitat loss.

issues.label: Hard look at environmental impacts
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether NEPA analysis took a hard look at direct, indirect, and cumulative impacts.

issues.label: Range of reasonable alternatives
issues.why: Court must determine whether the agency considered reasonable alternatives, including reduced take, different mitigation, or no action.

issues.label: No-action alternative analysis
issues.why: Court must ensure NEPA analysis meaningfully evaluated the no-action baseline compared to the Plan/permits.

issues.label: Segmentation/connected actions
issues.why: Court must assess whether the Plan, master permits, and certificates constitute connected actions requiring unified NEPA review.

issues.label: Tiering/programmatic NEPA adequacy
issues.why: Court must decide whether programmatic analysis is adequate or site-specific analysis was required before authorizing take.

issues.label: Site-specific impacts deferred
issues.why: Court must determine whether deferring specifics to certificates/individual projects unlawfully postpones NEPA analysis.

issues.label: Cumulative impacts of many projects
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether NEPA adequately assessed cumulative impacts from multiple developments over ten years.

issues.label: Indirect effects of development
issues.why: Court must assess whether NEPA considered indirect effects like fragmentation, increased human activity, and long-term habitat degradation.

issues.label: Mitigation in NEPA analysis
issues.why: Court must decide whether mitigation measures are sufficiently definite to support a FONSI and reduce significance.

issues.label: Mitigation monitoring under NEPA
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether NEPA adequately addresses monitoring/enforcement of mitigation relied upon to avoid an EIS.

issues.label: Scientific integrity under NEPA
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Service used high-quality science and disclosed data limitations and uncertainties.

issues.label: Public involvement requirements
issues.why: Court must assess whether NEPA/ESA public notice and comment requirements were satisfied for the Plan and permits.

issues.label: Consideration of comments
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Service responded to significant comments and criticisms in the administrative record.

issues.label: Environmental justice/community effects
issues.why: Court must consider whether NEPA required analysis of disproportionate impacts to communities, if raised and relevant.

issues.label: Climate and growth assumptions
issues.why: Court must decide whether foreseeable population growth/economic changes and related habitat pressures were reasonably analyzed.

issues.label: Consistency with recovery planning
issues.why: Court must assess whether authorized take and mitigation align with any recovery plan goals and priorities.

issues.label: Reliance on future actions
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the Service improperly relied on uncertain future land protection or funding commitments.

issues.label: Arbitrary-and-capricious explanation
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Service provided a reasoned explanation connecting facts to its ESA/NEPA conclusions.

issues.label: Consideration of relevant factors
issues.why: Court must assess whether the agency ignored important aspects (e.g., mitigation failure rates, unit-level impacts).

issues.label: Rational connection to evidence
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether findings (offset, funding, no significant impact) are supported by record evidence.

issues.label: Consistency across findings
issues.why: Court must check for internal inconsistency between projected habitat loss, take authorization, and claimed full offset.

issues.label: Potential need for injunction
issues.why: Court must decide whether to enjoin ongoing takes pending remand based on likelihood of harm and equitable factors.

issues.label: Vacatur versus remand without vacatur
issues.why: Court must weigh seriousness of errors and disruptive consequences in choosing the appropriate APA remedy.

issues.label: Attorneys’ fees eligibility
issues.why: Court must consider whether plaintiffs may recover fees under applicable fee-shifting provisions if they prevail.
